summary: An 80-ft tower on Chestnut Ridge in Forbes State Forest, built 1935, closed to the public and in need of major repairs.

facts.design: Constructed by the Marshal McClintock Company; erected by Civilian Conservation Corps crews (register)

access.note: Closed to the general public for several years as of 2016 (Herald-Standard). TribLIVE also says it is closed to the public and locked when not in use. The register says the stairs would need replacing before any public reopening.

events.note: Constructed by the Marshal McClintock Company and erected by CCC crews. TribLIVE gives 1937 as the erection year.

Sources disagree on the last staffed year. TribLIVE quotes an inspector: someone was there until the 1960s. The register says staffed until the 1970s. The Herald-Standard says unmanned since the 1960s.
Closed to the general public for several years as of the 2016 Herald-Standard report
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 1765, PA 72
Register visit report (Dec 27, 2024): stairs rough but usable, cab ceiling caving slightly, tower and cabin need major repairs

corrections.why: The register attributes construction to the Marshal McClintock Company and erection to CCC crews. None of the sources read name Aermotor for this tower. Confirm the maker before accepting.

Fire tower stands guard over Forbes State Forest

notes_for_editor: Build year: 1935 (register, Herald-Standard) vs erected 1937 (TribLIVE). Last staffing: 1960s (TribLIVE, Herald-Standard) vs 1970s (register); the register's 2024 visit report says not staffed. Brief's Aermotor design is not supported by any source read; the register names the Marshal McClintock Company, so the correction is proposed for review. Access: closed to the public per the 2016 Herald-Standard and TribLIVE (undated in the text; TribLIVE also notes an open house each fall for the grounds). The 2024 register visit implies it is still not open. The current status was not checked beyond the register. Do not encourage climbing.
